title: USB CDC, MSC, and MIDI: console, storage, and music

spans.text: USB CDC provides a serial console, MSC exposes block storage to a host, and USB MIDI sends musical control events to a computer.

USB CDC creates a virtual COM port; bound command-line length and keep parsing non-blocking. USB MSC needs sector (LBA) `onRead`/`onWrite` callbacks. When sharing an SD card as MSC, the host and MCU must never write the same FAT filesystem at the same time: do not open MCU files while the host owns the disk, and safely eject on the host before taking it back. Raw-sector callbacks sit below the filesystem layer; safely detach/remount before local use. Sharing internal flash also requires a deliberate partition layout and wear strategy.

USB MIDI sends musical events such as note-on and control-change; it is not serial text. Use it for a button/potentiometer controller. Arduino-ESP32 provides `USBSerial`, `USBMSC`, and `USBMIDI` examples. A native USB peripheral and the correct USB Mode are required on boards such as ESP32-S2/S3; host OTG is a separate role with separate drivers.
CDC: read a command from the serial console
MSC: expose SD card sectors to the USB host
MIDI: start and stop a note with a button

spans.title: Important safety and compatibility note
spans.text: The MSC sketch uses raw sectors on a real card; never access `SD_MMC` files concurrently. Eject on the host before unplugging and reinitialize local filesystem access afterward. CDC/MIDI/MSC APIs depend on the exact board and Arduino core; verify the S2/S3 schematic and USB Mode.
